text:
Marissa Cole: trying to lock MVP scope for Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) so Console + policy + routing aren’t building two different things. Main Q: for beta, are we ok with *manual gates first* (operator verifies + clicks promote) vs requiring *automated gate eval* from day 1?

Marissa Cole: context: if we require full automated gates for beta, Console needs gate evidence panels + policy engine needs deterministic eval + telemetry tagging, and I’m worried we blow the March beta window.

Lauren Bishop: from Dedicated side, customers are basically asking for “don’t take me down when you upgrade the pool” more than “let me run experiments.” If we can give them stages + hold + rollback with clear audit log, that’s already a big step.

Lauren Bishop: but… the design partners are explicitly asking for objective signals (error/latency/429) as promotion criteria. If we show “manual gate” only, we need to be careful about how we position it.

Paula Mendes: agree. I’m leaning hybrid for MVP: automated gates for a small fixed set of metrics (error rate + p95 + saturation/queue depth) and *manual* for anything quality-related. Otherwise we’ll get stuck debating custom thresholds.

Marissa Cole: hybrid is fine, but what’s “small fixed set” for beta? If it’s only “gate: pass/fail + reason” without customer configurable thresholds, we can ship faster.

Lauren Bishop: for Lattice AI (the one Liam’s working), they said: “give us canary 1% with rollback if 429s spike.” That’s basically automated 429/error gate.

Liam O'Rourke: yep. They also asked for “no promote if latency regresses > X%” but they’ll accept Redwood defaults for beta if we explain it.

Talia Benson: can we make an explicit decision today so I can update the Phase 1/2 milestones? Right now the plan doc says Phase 1 = routing primitives + manual gates, Phase 2 = automated gates + dashboards.

Paula Mendes: my worry w/ “manual gates only” beta is we’ll still get paged in practice because nobody wants to eyeball 6 dashboards at 2am. Even if it’s operator-driven, they’ll ask for “tell me when it’s safe.”

Marissa Cole: totally. But if we do automated gates in beta, we need to define missing-metrics behavior. If telemetry lags, do we block promotion? That could cause “stuck rollout” which is also bad.

Lauren Bishop: I’d rather have “stuck but safe” than “promote blind.” Dedicated customers will accept friction if we have an escape hatch.

Marissa Cole: so: fail-closed on missing data + allow force-promote for admin? (with scary confirmation + audit)

Paula Mendes: +1. MVP gate evaluation proposal:
- error rate (5xx + model errors) over 5m window
- request drop / 429 rate over 5m
- p95 latency over 5m (relative delta vs baseline stage)
- saturation/headroom (GPU util / queue depth) over 5m
- minimum sample size (if too few requests, gate = “insufficient data” -> treat as fail unless force)

Paula Mendes: keep thresholds Redwood-defined per tier for beta. No customer tuning.

Kenji Nakamura: from UX: if we do manual-only, the stage timeline still needs a “gate checklist” UI anyway (people will ask “what am I supposed to check?”). If we do automated, we can show results + “why failed” and it’s actually simpler for users.

Marissa Cole: ok that’s a good point. I don’t want a UI that’s just “trust me bro click promote.”

Lauren Bishop: also: customer commitments. We told HarborBank (regulated) “auditable change control w/ gated rollout.” If it’s all manual with no recorded evidence, that’s not going to pass their internal review.

Marissa Cole: we can still audit manual approvals (who clicked promote, reason). But yes, having objective gate output is stronger.

Talia Benson: can we frame as:
MVP beta = automated gates for a fixed set of platform SLO metrics (Redwood-defined), with manual override.
GA = more complete gate evidence + dashboards + optional quality gates integration.

Paula Mendes: that matches what I’ve been saying. Biggest open is stage defaults + how many stages we support in beta. I’m pushing 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% (4 stages) + optional 0% “draft.”

Lauren Bishop: agree. Also for small pools we may need replica-based partitioning instead of strict % traffic, but that’s implementation detail. Product can just call it “canary” etc.

Marissa Cole: re timeline: if we do automated gates in beta, I need engineering to commit that the gate evidence API won’t churn. Console can build on a stable contract.

Paula Mendes: I can write down the gate result schema today and share w/ Chloe/Jada. Should be stable: query window, observed value, threshold, pass/fail, and a text reason.

Kenji Nakamura: UX copy suggestion: “Gate evaluation (automatic)” vs “Manual verification,” and show override as “Force promote (admin)” with callouts.

Liam O'Rourke: customer-facing: Lattice will be ok if we tell them “beta uses standard Redwood gates; advanced tuning later.” They mostly want rollback safety + not starving capacity.

Lauren Bishop: so decision: no “manual-only” beta. We do basic automated gates + override + hold.

Marissa Cole: I’m good with that if we explicitly keep scope tight:
- v1 gates limited to latency/error/429/saturation/headroom
- no customer custom metrics
- no custom thresholds
- quality gates optional/manual

Paula Mendes: +1. Also we should decide how long the eval window is (5m vs 15m). Product POV: I’d prefer 5m default + require min sample size, so it doesn’t block low-traffic pools forever.

Lauren Bishop: 5m default works for most Dedicated traffic. For batchy workloads we’ll need a workaround (force promote / extend window) but that’s okay for beta.

Talia Benson: capturing action items:
1) Marissa/Paula: document MVP gates + override semantics + stage defaults in PRD section by EOD tomorrow.
2) Kenji: update wireframes to reflect “automatic gates + override” (not manual-only).
3) Liam: confirm with Lattice AI that Redwood-defined gates are acceptable for beta + target beta date.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: I’ll update the PRD + Slack Ethan/Jordan that product is committing to automated gates in beta (fixed set, fail-closed, admin override).

Lauren Bishop: thanks. Also pls call out in PRD that we need clear “hold” state (customer asked for pause during peak hours) and that promotion should be reversible.

Paula Mendes: will add. Also adding an explicit “insufficient data” state so we don’t pretend it’s passing.

Kenji Nakamura: sounds good. I’ll post updated timeline component mocks in the design thread once ready.

Talia Benson: cool. I’ll update the cross-team schedule: beta still late March if we hold scope, otherwise slips to April.

Marissa Cole: aligned. Let’s keep beta promise realistic: staged rollout safety, not a full experiment platform.
